mainTopic: Girls whose vows no one can cancel, a husband cancelling his wife's conditional vows, and a man's conditional vow about marrying
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's list of girls whose נדרים stand because neither a father nor a husband can cancel them. רבי יהודה adds a girl who was married off young and came back home widowed or divorced. The גמרא quotes רב, who says the long list follows רבי יהודה, while the חכמים group everything into three types: a בוגרת, a יתומה, and a יתומה בחיי האב. A new משנה teaches that a husband can cancel his wife's vow when it depends on whether she prepares things for him or for the fathers. A ברייתא shows that רבי נתן disagrees, both in that case and in a vow that would forbid her to all Jews if she is intimate with her husband. The חכמים say the husband can cancel both. The amud ends with a story about a man who vowed not to marry before learning הלכה. He was misled into marrying anyway, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the list of girls whose vows stand
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of girls whose vows cannot be canceled, giving cases that mix age (נערה or בוגרת) with whether the father is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: These vows also stand: a young girl not yet grown who is an orphan; a grown woman whose father died; a girl who became grown and then her father died; a young girl not yet grown whose father died; a girl whose father died and who grew up after he died; a grown woman whose father is alive; a girl who became grown while her father is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list, begun on the previous דף, of girls whose vows stand and cannot be canceled by anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is built from two facts: her age stage (נערה or בוגרת) and whether her father is alive. In every case on this list, the father has no power over her vows. This happens either because he died or because she is already a בוגרת, and so her vow stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl in the short stage just after childhood, when her father still has power over her vows
A girl who has fully grown up, so her father no longer controls her vows
An orphan; here, a girl whose father has died

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings of קיים. Here, אביה קיים means 'her father is alive.' Later, נדריהן קיימין means 'their vows stand.'

phrases.english: A young girl who has not yet grown up, and she is an orphan.
A grown woman, and her father died.
A young girl who became a grown woman, and her father died.
A young girl who has not yet grown up, and her father died.
A young girl whose father died,
and after her father died, she grew up.
A grown woman, and her father is alive.
A young girl who became a grown woman, and her father is alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list from the previous דף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all these cases, the father has no power over her vows, so they stand.

steps.title: A daughter married young who came back home
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds a case: a father married off his young daughter, and she was widowed or divorced and came back to him. She is still a נערה by age, yet her vows stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even a man who married off his young daughter, and she became a widow or was divorced and came back to him, while she is still a נערה, is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds one more girl to the list of those whose vows stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once she is back in her father's house as a נערה, he has power over her vows again. רבי יהודה says no. Once he married her off, his power ended, even though she is still young.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl, still a child

steps.whyThisMatters: This case is the source of the idea of a 'יתומה בחיי האב,' an orphan while her father is alive, which the גמרא uses in the next step.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
Even one who married off his young daughter,
and she became a widow or was divorced,
and she came back to him,
and she is still a young girl.
phrases.notes: He means that even though she is still a נערה, her vows stand, because her father's power ended when he married her off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ הַקְּטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter who was married off and came back widowed or divorced is no longer under her father's power over vows.

steps.title: The long list is רבי יהודה's view; the חכמים give three categories
steps.stepSummary: רב says the whole detailed משנה follows רבי יהודה. The חכמים simply say three kinds of girls have vows that stand: a בוגרת, a יתומה, and a יתומה בחיי האב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the opinion of רבי יהודה. But the חכמים say there are three girls whose vows stand: a grown woman, an orphan, and an 'orphan while her father is alive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us who wrote the long list in the משנה, and it gives the חכמים' shorter version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה spelled out every combination one by one. The חכמים grouped them into three types. The third type, יתומה בחיי האב, is the girl from רבי יהודה's case: her father is alive, but he lost his power over her when he married her off, so for vows she counts like an orphan.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Their vows stand and cannot be canceled
An 'orphan while her father is alive': a girl whose father lost his power over her because she was married off

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, three girls have vows that stand: a בוגרת, a יתומה, and a יתומה בחיי האב.

phrases.english: גמרא: רב יהודה said that רב said:
This is the opinion of רבי יהודה.
But the חכמים say:
There are three young girls whose vows stand:
a grown woman, and an orphan,
and an orphan during her father's lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us whose view the משנה follows and gives the opposing summary
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The detailed list follows רבי יהודה. The חכמים count three categories: בוגרת, יתומה, and יתומה בחיי האב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two views reach the same kinds of cases. The חכמים simply group them into three categories.

steps.title: A wife's vow tied to preparing things for others
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A wife forbids herself benefit from her father or her husband's father if she prepares things for her husband, or she forbids benefit from her husband if she prepares things for the fathers. Either way, the husband can cancel the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a wife says: 'Benefit from my father and your father is קונם for me if I prepare anything for you,' or 'Benefit from you is forbidden to me if I prepare anything for my father or your father,' the husband can cancel the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a wife's vow that depends on a condition about preparing things for her husband or for the fathers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These vows only take effect if she does the act in the condition, so right now they are not yet in force. Even so, the משנה says the husband can cancel them now, before the condition is met. The ברייתא in the next step shows that רבי נתן disagrees on exactly this point.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used for a vow that makes something forbidden, like a קרבן
Literally 'for your mouth': preparing food or things for you

phrases.english: משנה: 'It is קונם, so that I may not benefit'
from my father and from your father
if I prepare anything for you,'
phrases.notes: Literally 'for your mouth.' She means preparing food or doing work for her husband.

phrases.english: or 'that I may not benefit from you'

phrases.aramaic: אִם עוֹשָׂה אֲנִי עַל פִּי אַבָּא
phrases.english: if I prepare anything for my father
or for your father' —
in such a case, he can cancel the vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֻוֽנָּם שֶׁאֵינִי נֶהֱנֶה לְאַבָּא וּלְאָבִיךָ אִם עוֹשָׂה אֲנִי עַל פִּיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a different topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband can cancel his wife's vow that depends on her preparing things for him or for the fathers.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי נתן says he cannot cancel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings the first case of the משנה. רבי נתן says the husband cannot cancel the vow, while the חכמים say he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If she says, 'I may not benefit from my father or your father if I prepare anything for you,' רבי נתן says he cannot cancel it, and the חכמים say he can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the משנה's ruling is not agreed by everyone. רבי נתן disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן holds that the husband cannot cancel this vow. It has not taken effect yet, and it only depends on whether she prepares things for him. The חכמים say he can cancel it anyway, which matches what our משנה ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For you,' the same idea as על פיך

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה, which lets the husband cancel, follows the חכמים. רבי נתן says he cannot cancel this conditional vow.

phrases.english: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא:
'That I may not benefit from my father or from your father'
if I prepare anything for you,'
רבי נתן says: he cannot cancel the vow.
And the חכמים say: he can cancel the vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: שֶׁאֵינִי נֶהֱנֵית לְאַבָּא וּלְאָבִיךְ אִם אֲנִי עוֹשָׂה לְפִיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing a disagreement about the משנה's first case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נתן: the husband cannot cancel. חכמים: he can.

steps.title: Second case of the teaching: a vow that would forbid her to all Jews
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a second wife's vow: 'I am removed from the Jews if I am intimate with you.' רבי נתן says the husband cannot cancel it, and the חכמים say he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said, 'I am removed from the Jews if I am intimate with you,' רבי נתן says the husband cannot cancel the vow, and the חכמים say he can cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from step 5 with a second vow case. The same two sides argue again: רבי נתן says no הפרה, and the חכמים say the husband can cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wife's vow takes effect only if she is intimate with her husband. If it does, being with her becomes forbidden to all Jews. The argument has the same shape as the first case: רבי נתן says the husband cannot cancel this kind of vow, while the חכמים say he can.

keyTerms.meaning: I am removed / taken away; she makes herself off-limits
The Jews; here, every Jewish man

phrases.english: "I am removed from the Jews
phrases.notes: She means that being with her will be forbidden to every Jewish man.

phrases.english: if I am intimate with you,"
Rabbi Natan says: he cannot cancel it.
And the Sages say: he can cancel it.

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases of the ברייתא, רבי נתן says the husband cannot cancel, and the חכמים say he can.
steps.triggerLanguage: נְטוּלָה אֲנִי מִן הַיְּהוּדִים אִם מְשַׁמַּשְׁתֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 5 with its second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a vow forbidding herself to all Jews if she is with her husband: רבי נתן says no הפרה, and the חכמים say the husband can cancel.

steps.title: A man vows not to marry before learning, then is misled into marrying
steps.stepSummary: A man vowed that all benefit in the world would be forbidden to him if he married before learning הלכה. He tried very hard but could not learn. רב אחא בר רב הונא misled him, and he married.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who forbade himself all benefit in the world if he married a woman before learning הלכה. He tried with all his strength but could not learn. רב אחא בר רב הונא came, misled him, and he married a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a man's vow. This sets up a question that the story takes up on the next amud: what happens to his vow now that he married?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's vow depended on a condition: marrying before he had learned הלכה. He married while that condition was still true, because רב אחא בר רב הונא led him astray. So his vow seems to have taken effect, and the story will continue to deal with that.

keyTerms.meaning: Ran with a ladder and rope; tried with all his strength

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the man broke his vow on purpose. He married because רב אחא בר רב הונא misled him.

phrases.english: There was a certain man
who forbade upon himself the benefit of the world
if he married a woman
while I have not learned הלכה.
phrases.notes: The words switch to 'I' because this is the wording of his own vow.

phrases.english: He ran with a ladder and a rope
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying he tried as hard as he possibly could.

phrases.english: but he was not able to learn.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna came
and misled him
phrases.notes: He let the man think the vow would not take effect.

phrases.english: and he married a woman,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאִיתְּסַר הֲנָיָיתָא דְּעָלְמָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about a vow that depends on a condition (marrying before learning הלכה). It continues the theme of the conditional vows argued over by רבי נתן and the חכמים in steps 5-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a man whose vow depended on marrying before learning הלכה married while that condition was still true.
